Tables list workspace vs global paths for 2.0, CLI, and IDE
Linked from official home docs and awesome-agent-skills lists as official documentation

Plugin marketplace completeness and pricing of Antigravity itself are not specified on this page

aiReview.description: Learn the Agent Skills standard, SKILL.md frontmatter, and where Antigravity 2.0, CLI, and IDE load workspace and global skills.

Defines the SKILL.md folder layout, required description frontmatter, and progressive disclosure.
Documents skill paths and invocation for Antigravity 2.0, CLI, and IDE, including plugins.
Notes backward compatibility for .agent/skills versus .agents/skills.

aiReview.summary: Community Python CLI that maps Claude Code/Cursor SKILL.md files to Antigravity plugins (tool names, GEMINI.md/AGENTS.md, plugin.json). Useful for skill migration, but it is unofficial, lightly starred, and writes into ~/.gemini config.
evidence: Repo description and README describe porting Claude Code/Cursor skills to Antigravity plugins.
Quickstart uses python port_skill.py with --dry-run and GitHub skill URLs.
Facts: MIT, not archived, 5 stars, pushed_at 2026-09-12.
Topics include google-antigravity, claude-skills, multi-agent.
uncertainty: Actual correctness of tool remapping and invoke_subagent injection was not executed.
Maintenance beyond the single 2026-09-12 push and example quality were not audited.
Security of ingesting arbitrary GitHub skill trees into user config was not reviewed.
aiReview.tagline: Convert Claude/Cursor skills into Antigravity plugins
aiReview.description: CLI that ingests SKILL.md sources, remaps tools and context files, and emits Antigravity plugin.json plus optional subagent wiring.
pros: Documents deterministic mappings from Claude tools and CLAUDE.md to Antigravity equivalents.
Supports GitHub URL, local SKILL.md, dry-run diffs, and global or workspace install paths.
MIT-licensed with example ports (llm-council, frontend-design, multi-skill bundle).

cons: Not official Google Antigravity documentation; five stars and two forks.
README is promotional and claims optimizer/transpiler behavior that is not independently verified.
Installs into global ~/.gemini/config unless --workspace is used.

reference.excerpt:
# 🚀 Antigravity Skill Porter & Optimizer

> **Bridge the AI Agent Ecosystem:** The ultimate transpiler and optimizer that imports, converts, and elevates agent skills from **Claude Code**, **Cursor**, and **OpenAI** into high-performance, native **Google Antigravity (AGY)** plugins and multi-agent workflows.

---

## 💡 Why This Exists

The AI agent community is experiencing rapid innovation, with developers publishing thousands of open-standard `SKILL.md` workflows for Claude Code and Cursor.

However, running external skills inside Google Antigravity naively creates severe friction:
- ❌ **Tool Hallucinations**: External skills hardcode Claude-specific tools (`Bash`, `Glob`, `Read`, `Edit`, `StrReplaceEditor`) which fail or cause confusion in Antigravity.
- ❌ **Context Blindness**: They search for `CLAUDE.md`, ignoring Antigravity's `GEMINI.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and hierarchical `.agents/rules/`.

aiReview.summary: This is a low-star fork of sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills (also branded as an Antigravity skills catalog), not official Google Antigravity docs. Prefer the upstream catalog or official skill sources over this clone.
evidence: canonicalUrl is github.com/kench001/antigravity-awesome-skills; page states forked from sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills.

Rubric prefers official Antigravity docs and maintained GitHub skills over template clones.

Whether community skills include unsafe or low-quality playbooks.
Exact overlap with other awesome-skills listings already in the directory.
aiReview.tagline: Forked SKILL.md catalog and installer for AI coding agents
aiReview.description: Installable SKILL.md library, CLI, bundles, and workflows for Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, and similar tools.
pros: README documents an npm installer, SKILL.md catalog, bundles, workflows, and multi-tool install paths.
Repository includes LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, catalog, and skills directories.
Upstream lineage is a large maintained skills collection (parent sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills).

README still points stars, releases, and badges at the sickn33 upstream, so this listing is a clone.
Skill quality and Antigravity-specific maintenance cannot be verified from this fork alone.

aiReview.summary: Community MIT vault of 300+ Google Antigravity agent skills ported from Claude Code, with CLI, catalog, and bundles. Not official antigravity.google docs, but a maintained GitHub skills collection rather than a generic clone or search result.
evidence: GitHub description: curated Agent Skills for Google Antigravity; topics antigravity and antigravity-skills.
README: skills/ directory, npm run build:catalog, skills_cli.py, plugin.json.
Stars ~1.8k, forks 276, MIT license listed on the repo page.
uncertainty: Skill quality and Antigravity compatibility of individual ports were not audited file-by-file.
Maintenance cadence beyond 40 commits on main was not verified in detail.
aiReview.tagline: 300+ ported agent skills with CLI catalog and bundles
aiReview.description: Install curated Antigravity skills from a catalog and CLI, covering development, ops, security, and workflows without loading every skill at once.
pros: Public GitHub repo with MIT license, README, CATALOG.md, tests, changelog, and security policy.
Documents 300+ skills plus catalog.json, bundles.json, aliases, and a Python/npm CLI for targeted install.
About 1.8k stars, 276 forks, and 40 commits indicate active community use.
Warns that installing all skills increases token use and prefers search, tags, or bundles.
cons: Unofficial port of Claude Code agents, not Google Antigravity first-party docs.
Large skill surface can still cause irrelevant auto-activation if users ignore targeted install guidance.

aiReview.summary: Community Python CLI that orchestrates workspaces and injects skills from antigravity-awesome-skills via wizard, symlinks, and sync. Useful companion tooling, not official Google Antigravity docs.
evidence: GitHub description and README: CLI to orchestrate workspaces and inject skills from sickn33/antigravity-awesome-skills.
Repo stats: public, MIT, 16 stars, 1 fork, 15 commits, files include workspace-manager.py and install.sh.
Discovered repeatedly from sickn33/antigravity-awesome-skills curated README, not official Google sources.
uncertainty: Runtime quality, test coverage, and safety of install.sh/sync clone behavior not independently verified.
Depth of actual Antigravity IDE integration versus generic .agent/skills layout is unclear.
aiReview.tagline: CLI to isolate workspaces and inject agent skills
aiReview.description: Create isolated workspaces and inject selected skills into Antigravity, Claude Code, and Cursor via a Python CLI wizard and sync.
pros: MIT-licensed Python CLI with documented commands such as wsm init, wizard, enable, disable, and sync.
Documents workspace isolation via skill-config.json and per-project skill symlinks.
Includes English and Spanish READMEs, install.sh, and demo GIFs.
Targets Antigravity plus Claude Code and Cursor skill/context loading.
cons: Third-party companion with 16 stars, 1 fork, and 15 commits, not official antigravity.google docs.
Recommended install pipes curl into bash.
Manual install docs mention wsm init before describing how the wsm alias is created.
Depends on the community antigravity-awesome-skills catalog rather than maintained Google skills.

aiReview.summary: Community CLI and skill/agent/command pack that lists Antigravity among many assistants; not official Google Antigravity docs. Canonical URL redirects to guanyang/open-agent-hub.
evidence: GitHub page title and description: lightweight zero-dependency CLI for AI coding assistants.
Compatibility table includes Antigravity IDE with project .agents/ and global ~/.gemini/antigravity/.
README lists 83+ skills, agents/, commands/, scripts/hub.js, MIT license, ~977 stars.
uncertainty: Whether the awesome list still intends the old antigravity-skills name.
Depth of real Antigravity testing versus Claude/Cursor-first design.
Currency of all 83+ skills versus the 223-commit main branch.
aiReview.tagline: Zero-dep CLI to link skills, agents, and commands
aiReview.description: Install and link Markdown skills, agents, and slash commands into Claude, Cursor, Antigravity, Gemini, and similar coding assistants.
pros: MIT-licensed repo with README, changelog, contributing, and security docs.
Documents full path mapping for Antigravity (.agents/ and ~/.gemini/antigravity/).
Includes a skills catalog, agent/command guidelines, and a zero-dependency oah CLI.
cons: github.com/guanyang/antigravity-skills redirects to open-agent-hub, so the listed name is stale.
It is a multi-tool community hub, not official antigravity.google documentation.
Skills are third-party prompt packs; quality and Antigravity-specific maintenance vary.

aiReview.summary: Community fork of sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills: a large SKILL.md catalog plus installer CLI aimed at many agent IDEs, including Antigravity. Not official Google Antigravity docs; treat as a third-party clone of a multi-tool skills library.
evidence: canonicalUrl is github.com/iradoweck/antigravity-awesome-skills; page states forked from sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills.

uncertainty: How far this fork diverges from the parent (stale vs. unique Antigravity content).
Safety and quality of individual community SKILL.md files and installer behavior.
License of aggregated third-party skill content beyond MIT on the repo.
aiReview.tagline: Installable SKILL.md catalog and CLI for many agent IDEs
aiReview.description: Browse and install community SKILL.md playbooks for Claude, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, and similar tools.

Lists license, security, contributing, and code-of-conduct files.
States compatibility with Antigravity among several agent CLIs and IDEs.
cons: GitHub metadata shows this is a fork of sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills, not an official Antigravity project.
The fork has far fewer stars than a primary listing and README still points at the parent project.
Apply/recovery paths are described as experimental; catalog quality of 2,000+ community skills is not independently verified.

aiReview.summary: Community Antigravity-first kit of rules, skills, specialist agents, workflows, and a CLI installer; popular and documented but not official Google docs.
evidence: README describes Antigravity as primary runtime and documents .agents rules/skills/workflows, 20 role definitions, PreToolUse hook, and ag-kit CLI.
GitHub shows MIT license, ~8k stars on ag-kit, npm package @vudovn/ag-kit.

uncertainty: Exact current star/commit counts on the old antigravity-kit name vs ag-kit.
Quality and originality of individual skill files vs official Google skills.
Whether default MCP examples with YOUR_API_KEY are commonly left unconfigured in the wild.
aiReview.tagline: Antigravity workspace kit: skills, agents, workflows, CLI
aiReview.description: Installs a .agents workspace with skills, specialist routing, workflows, memory, MCP guidance, and a narrow PreToolUse safety hook for Google Antigravity.
pros: MIT-licensed GitHub project with substantial stars/forks and a documented Antigravity-first production profile.
Provides npx/npm CLI install, merge-aware updates, backups, and workspace verification commands.
Includes rules, skills, workflows, specialist routing, memory guidance, MCP helpers, and a narrow destructive-command gate.
Ships SECURITY.md, migration notes, and CI/doctor-style checks.
cons: Community toolkit, not official antigravity.google documentation.
Canonical URL antigravity-kit appears redirected/renamed to ag-kit; listing should track the live repo.
Runtime compatibility outside Antigravity is not guaranteed; Node 22 and a trusted workspace are required for full checks.

Live search-result contents, which change over time

aiReview.summary: Third-party MIT Python CLI/MCP that builds a local .repobrain knowledge layer and answers codebase questions with file citations; it was renamed from Antigravity Workspace Template and is not official Google Antigravity docs or skills.
evidence: GitHub API for study8677/antigravity-workspace-template resolves to study8677/repobrain (1325 stars, MIT, Python).
README subtitle: Formerly known as Antigravity Workspace Template.
Rubric prefers official antigravity.google docs and maintained GitHub skills over template clones.
uncertainty: Whether the awesome list intends Antigravity IDE templates versus this renamed knowledge engine.
Current redirect/canonical URL stability for github.com/study8677/antigravity-workspace-template.
Independence and reproducibility of the published CodeGraph comparison.
aiReview.tagline: Cross-IDE local knowledge base and grounded repo Q&A
aiReview.description: Build module knowledge in-repo, then ask questions with source paths via CLI, MCP, or IDE plugins.
pros: README documents rb-refresh and rb-ask, a .repobrain knowledge directory, MCP, and several IDE hosts.
MIT license, Python 3.10+, CI badge, tests, changelog, and multi-language docs are present.
Includes benchmark artifacts and a support matrix for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others.
cons: The listed URL is a former workspace-template name; the live project is RepoBrain, not official Antigravity.
First knowledge builds require a configured LLM and can take minutes on large repos.
README includes a third-party API-key/router promotion unrelated to the core tool.

aiReview.summary: Community Windows Codex MCP plugin that bridges OpenAI Codex (including ChatGPT mobile) to a local Antigravity 2.0 desktop app via CLI, DevTools, and PowerShell helpers. Related to Antigravity workflows but unofficial, Windows-only, and low-star; not official antigravity.google docs or a maintained Google skill pack.
evidence: GitHub description: Codex plugin connecting to a local Antigravity 2.0 desktop app.
README lists antigravity-local and antigravity-devtools MCP servers and PowerShell helpers.
Repo topics include antigravity, codex-plugin, connector; 35 commits, MIT license.
uncertainty: Runtime reliability of DevTools/UI automation was not verified.
Compatibility with current Antigravity/Codex plugin marketplace versions is unknown.
Code quality and security of PowerShell/MCP scripts were not audited line-by-line.
aiReview.tagline: Windows Codex MCP bridge to local Antigravity desktop
aiReview.description: Connect Codex to a local Windows Antigravity 2.0 app with MCP tools, CLI jobs, DevTools inspection, and chat handoff.
pros: README documents MCP tools, install path, Windows requirements, and job artifact folders.
Repository includes MIT license, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, and a skills/antigravity-2 path.
Prefers official agy CLI for headless work before driving the Electron UI via DevTools.
cons: Community plugin with only 5 stars and 2 forks; not official Google Antigravity documentation.
Limited to Windows and a hardcoded Antigravity.exe install path.
Drives a local Electron app through Chromium DevTools, which can be fragile and high-privilege on the host.
